compliance.title: Compliance profile
compliance.subtitle: the rules the system enforces, and who confirmed each one
compliance.banner: The software enforces these rules. It does not assert that they are the law. Each one names its source and the person who confirmed it — and until somebody does, it is marked unconfirmed and enforced as a warning only.
compliance.noRulesYet: No rules are written down yet. A rule nobody has written down cannot be confirmed — and a system that invents the rule at the moment it needs it is a system asserting a law on its own authority.
compliance.seeded: The rules are written down. None of them is confirmed except the ones a decree confirms itself.
compliance.decreeConfirmsItself: A decree confirms itself. There is nothing for a person to add, and nothing to take back.
compliance.whoSaidSoHint: your accountant's name, or your own
compliance.confirmIt: Confirm — it will refuse from now on
compliance.whyTakeItBackHint: a finance act changed it, the question was wrong…
compliance.nowBlocks: Confirmed. From now on a document that fails this rule is refused, not warned about.
compliance.nowWarns: Taken back. It warns again, and documents already issued are untouched.
compliance.structural: What the system does whatever anybody says
compliance.structuralWhat: guarantees that come from how it is built
compliance.structuralWhy: These are not rules somebody confirmed — they are properties of the code, and there is no switch for them. They are listed because a reader asking what this software enforces deserves the whole answer.

built.chronological: Numbers documents in order, with no gaps
built.neverReuse: Never gives out the same number twice, even under two people issuing at once
built.neverEditIssued: Never edits an issued document — a correction is a new document
built.oneRenderer: Draws every document with one renderer, so they cannot drift apart
built.numberOnIssue: Takes a number at issue and never on a draft
built.amountInWords: Writes the amount in words in the document's own language

compliance.principleWhy: why the wording changed across the whole system
compliance.principleQuote: Software should not tell you what the law is. It should do what you told it to do, and show you who told it.
compliance.principleBody: Screens used to say things like "required by art. 42 CTCA". That is the software making a legal claim, and if the claim is wrong — or the article is renumbered in a finance act — the software is confidently wrong in a place nobody thinks to check. Every one of those strings now reads from this profile. The behaviour is identical: the invoice is still refused without a NIF. What changed is that the reason is attributed, dated and reviewable, and an unconfirmed rule warns instead of blocking.

nif.was: "The client NIF is missing and article 42 of the CTCA requires it on every invoice."
nif.now: "Cannot issue — the client NIF is missing. Rule from décret exécutif 05-468, confirmed by the decree itself."

mentions.was: "décret exécutif 05-468 · the system refuses to issue without them"
mentions.now: "The required mentions, from your Algeria profile. Confirmed ones refuse; the rest warn."

stamp.now: "Stamp duty on cash settlement — nobody has confirmed the rule, so this is a warning."

compliance.whatToDoBody: Export it, send it to your accountant, and have him confirm or correct the unconfirmed rules. It is one page. That conversation is worth having once, and this is the artefact that makes it a fifteen-minute conversation instead of a research project.
compliance.reversibleBody: A confirmation is somebody's judgement, and judgements get revised — a finance act moves a threshold, or the wrong question was asked. Taking one back changes what happens next, never what already happened: a document issued under the old rule keeps its number and its content.
compliance.seeDayOne: See it on the day-one checklist

error.noSuchRule: That rule is not in the profile.

onePager.title: Compliance profile — questions for our accountant
onePager.intro: Our invoicing software refuses to issue a document that breaks a rule we have confirmed, and warns about one we have not. Below are the rules it does not yet act on, because nobody qualified has told us what they are. Each one takes a sentence to settle. Everything already settled is listed underneath, so you can correct it if we have it wrong.

error.exceedsPayment: That allocates more than the payment received.
error.exceedsBalance: That is more than this invoice still owes.

convert.createsADraft: Creates a draft. Nothing is issued and no number is reserved.
convert.neverReplaced: The proforma is never replaced. It stays on file, linked to the facture, and its number is not reused.
convert.ownNumber: every step keeps its own number
convert.chainNote: The same chain applies whatever the client is. A devis can go straight to a facture, a proforma can be skipped, a situation replaces the facture on works — the steps are configurable, the numbering rules are not.
convert.nOpen: {n, plural, =0 {nothing left to decide} one {# still to decide} other {# still to decide}}

value.nLines: {n, plural, one {# line} other {# lines}}, {total} excl. VAT

value.nOptions: {n, plural, =0 {none} one {# line not counted} other {# lines not counted}}
value.mentionsBlocked: {n, plural, one {# rule refuses} other {# rules refuse}}

convert.stampDutyNote: Stamp duty is only added once the accountant has confirmed the rule on the Compliance screen. Until then a cash settlement is flagged at issue and nothing is computed.
convert.nToFix: {n, plural, one {# to fix} other {# to fix}}
convert.noRules: No rule applies to this document type yet.

error.notIssued: That document has never been issued, so there is nothing to preserve. Edit it instead.
error.conversionNotAllowed: That conversion is not one of the allowed ones.
error.alreadyConverted: This document has already been converted once.
error.nothingToCopy: There is nothing on this document to carry over.

convert.stampDutyApplied: Rule confirmed: a cash settlement carries stamp duty on the scale, computed on the total including VAT, when the draft is saved.

deliveries.title: Deliveries
deliveries.subtitle: {n, plural, =0 {No delivery note yet} one {# delivery note} other {# delivery notes}} · {unsigned, plural, =0 {every signed copy is on file} one {# without a signed copy} other {# without a signed copy}}
deliveries.empty: No delivery note has been created yet.
deliveries.notDispatchedYet: Nothing has gone out yet, so there is nothing to sign for.
deliveries.noProof: {n, plural, one {Delivery {numbers} has} other {{n} deliveries — {numbers} — have}} no signed proof on file. Without it a delivery dispute has no answer.
deliveries.whyItMatters: Without a signed delivery note, a delivery dispute has no answer. This is the document that protects the invoice.
deliveries.bothWays: A delivery note can be issued without an invoice, and one invoice can cover several delivery notes. The link is kept both ways.
deliveries.remainderFollows: the remainder follows on the next one
deliveries.noSource: This delivery note is not linked to a document.
deliveries.issuedIsFrozen: This delivery note has been issued. A correction is a new document.
deliveries.signedOnce: Recorded once. A second signing would overwrite the record of the first, and in a dispute the first is the one that matters.
deliveries.blockedNOpen: {n, plural, one {Blocked — # line open} other {Blocked — # lines open}}
deliveries.createsADraft: Creates a draft with no number. It is issued like any other document.
deliveries.defaultsToRemaining: defaults to what is still owed, not to what was ordered

error.sourceNotIssued: That document has never been issued, so there is nothing to deliver against.
error.nothingToDeliver: Enter a quantity on at least one line.
error.quantityNotPositive: A delivered quantity has to be greater than zero.
error.alreadySigned: A signed copy is already on file for this delivery note.

newInvoice.title: New invoice — from {number}
newInvoice.checkDontRetype: most of this is already known · check it rather than type it
newInvoice.createsADraft: Creates a draft. It is issued on the document screen, where the number is reserved.
newInvoice.nothingLeft: Every line has already been invoiced.
newInvoice.partialBanner: {n} of {m} lines are delivered. You can invoice those now, or wait for the rest — invoicing what is delivered is the faster route to cash.
newInvoice.carried: Carried over — check, do not retype
newInvoice.numberingNote: The number is reserved inside the transaction that issues the document, so the register stays gapless. Until then this is what it will look like, not what it will be.
newInvoice.sameMachine: the same machine as every other document
newInvoice.lifecycleNote: Draft and Issued are stored on the document. Partly paid and Paid are not — they are worked out from the payments allocated against it, and change without anybody touching the invoice. Overdue is not a state either: it is a date passing while a balance is still owed. Cancelling an issued invoice is a credit note, never a status change.

error.sourceNotIssued: That document has never been issued, so there is nothing to invoice from.
error.nothingLeftToBill: There is nothing left to invoice on that document.
error.nothingDelivered: Nothing has been delivered against it yet.
error.nothingChosen: Enter a quantity on at least one line.

today.headline: {n, plural, one {# thing needs you today} other {# things need you today}} · about {minutes} minutes
today.nothingNeedsYou: Nothing needs a decision from you today.

bandWhy.nowOrLost: deadlines that expire today or tomorrow
bandWhy.money: things that decide whether cash arrives
bandWhy.waitingOnYou: they cannot move until you answer
bandWhy.quick: clear these and the day is done

today.allClear: Nothing needs a decision from you
today.waitingElsewhere: {n, plural, one {# thing is waiting on somebody else} other {# things are waiting on other people}} — they are on the Waiting on page and come back to you when they move.
today.nothingWaitingElsewhere: Nothing is waiting on anybody else either.
today.doneFromLog: Taken from the audit log, not from a checkbox — this is what the system saw happen, not what somebody said they did.
today.nothingLater: Nothing else has a date this week.
today.howItIsBuiltBody: Ordered by what it costs you to ignore it, not by when it arrived. A deadline that expires tomorrow outranks an email from this morning. Anything waiting on somebody else is kept off this page on purpose.
today.noTaskTable: Nothing here is a task somebody created. Every line is read from a fact another screen already holds, so when the payment lands or the signed copy comes back, the line is simply gone — there is nothing to tick and nothing to tidy up.

waiting.title: Waiting on
waiting.subtitle: {n, plural, =0 {Nothing is sitting with anybody else} one {# thing sitting with somebody else} other {# things sitting with other people}} · {overdue, plural, =0 {none has been quiet too long} one {# has been quiet too long} other {# have been quiet too long}}
waiting.nothingNeedsYou: Nothing on this page needs you today. It is here so that when someone goes quiet, you find out before it costs you.
waiting.nobodyOwesAnything: Nobody owes you an answer at the moment.

groupWhat.supplier: a quote we asked for and have not received
groupWhat.client: a decision, a document or money

waiting.thresholdNote: Anything quiet for {n} days or more in this group is marked red. The three groups keep different clocks on purpose: a supplier silent for three days is slow, a bank silent for three days is normal.
waiting.whatIsMissing: What is not on this page yet
waiting.authoritiesLater: The frame shows a third group — authorities and banks, for things like a caution de soumission or a CASNOS attestation. Those are compliance documents and that module is not built, so nothing here knows a bank guarantee was ever requested. An empty group would read as “nothing outstanding”, which is the opposite of what is true.

week.title: Week ahead
week.summary: {deadlines, plural, =0 {no deadline} one {# deadline} other {# deadlines}} · {deliveries, plural, =0 {no delivery to prove} one {# delivery to prove} other {# deliveries to prove}} · {chases, plural, =0 {nothing to chase} one {# chase due} other {# chases due}}
week.fixedOrMoves: What is fixed and what can move
week.movabilityNote: This is a property of the kind of thing, not of one item. A client's deadline is fixed because a client set it, and no amount of wishing about one particular tender changes that. The difference between a week that works and one that does not is usually which of these somebody realised they could shift.
week.noQuietDays: Every day this week has something on it.
week.busiestDay: {n} of the week's {total} dated items land on {day}. Anything you can pull forward is the difference between calm and rushed.
week.noRiskFigure: No “money at risk” figure. An enquiry has no value until somebody has priced it, and most of these have not been — a number meaning “the ones we happen to have priced” looks complete and is not.
week.nothingHiddenBody: Everything on this page also appears on Today when its day comes. This view exists so you can see a crowded Thursday on Monday, not so you have a second list to manage. It reads from exactly the same place Today does.

approvals.title: Approvals
approvals.subtitle: {n, plural, =0 {nothing waiting on you} one {# waiting on you} other {# waiting on you}} · {total, plural, =0 {nothing waiting at all} one {# waiting in total} other {# waiting in total}} · rules that stop an action, not just record it
approvals.logVsGate: The audit log records what happened. These rules stop it happening until someone with the authority agrees. Different jobs — the system needs both.
approvals.nothingWaiting: Nothing is waiting on a decision.
approvals.nothingWaitingWhy: A gate only appears here when somebody has actually run into one. Nothing is gated retrospectively, and an empty page means nothing has been blocked — not that the rules are off.
approvals.notYours: This one is not yours to decide.
approvals.declined: Declined. The draft stays — nothing is lost.
approvals.selfApprovalNote: You asked for this one yourself. Deciding it is allowed and will be recorded as a self-approval.

behaviourValue.draftStaysNothingLost: The draft stays, nothing is lost

approvals.oneManCompany: When one person is the company
approvals.oneManCompanyBody: If you are the Gérant and the Commercial at once, these gates cost you a click each. Keep them anyway. The value is not the second person — it is that six months later the audit log says why the margin was 11.4% on that job, and you are not reconstructing it from memory.

error.gateDisabled: That rule has been switched off.
error.notApprovable: Nobody can approve that. An issued document cannot be changed — a correction is a credit note.
error.justificationRequired: Say why, in your own words.
error.notYourDecision: That decision belongs to somebody else.
error.alreadyDecided: That one has already been decided.

timeline.everythingHere: everything about it is on this page
timeline.nEvents: {n, plural, =0 {no events} one {# event} other {# events}}
timeline.nothingYet: Nothing has happened on this enquiry yet.
timeline.onlyRecord: the only record of a thing the system never saw
timeline.dueGoesToToday: A date puts it on Today when it comes.
timeline.verbatim: Kept word for word. A tidied note is your later summary of what was said, not what was said.
timeline.replyLater: Nothing in this system sends yet. Write the reply from your own mail.
timeline.filesLater: File storage is not built yet.

lastMove.in: {n, plural, =0 {They wrote today — the ball is with you.} one {They wrote yesterday. The ball has been with you for # day.} other {They wrote # days ago. The ball has been with you that long.}}
lastMove.out: {n, plural, =0 {You wrote today — it is with them.} one {You wrote yesterday. It has been with them for # day.} other {You wrote # days ago. It has been with them that long.}}

timeline.whoMovedLastNote: Notes and system events are skipped. A folder being created is not somebody's move, and neither is writing a note to yourself.
timeline.nobodyHasMoved: Nothing has been sent or received on this enquiry yet.
timeline.noEventTable: There is no event table. Every row but a note is read from the record that already holds it — the message, the quote, the document, the log. A second copy of each would be two versions of every fact, and no way to tell which one happened on the day they disagree.

error.empty: A note with no words records that you opened the box.

message.noBody: This message arrived with no text — only a subject, or only attachments.
message.downgraded: The rule matched, but not confidently enough to act on its own. It is waiting for you to say.

conversations.subtitle: Everything a client or a supplier has said, in one place · {needReply, plural, =0 {nothing needs a reply} one {# needs a reply} other {# need a reply}}
conversations.none: Nothing here yet. Conversations appear as mail arrives.
conversations.pickOne: Pick a conversation on the left.
conversations.cannotSend: Replies are sent from Outlook, not from here. The ERP is allowed to READ one mailbox and nothing more — it cannot send mail on your behalf, by design. What it does instead is make sure nothing here goes quiet unnoticed.

notify.subtitle: {unread, plural, =0 {Nothing unread} one {# unread} other {# unread}} · grouped by what they block
notify.nothingUnread: There is nothing unread to mark.
notify.preferencesHelp: Switching a kind off hides it from this page only. The invoice is still overdue, and it still appears on Today, on the deal and on the invoice itself — a toggle should never be a way to lose money.
notify.inAppOnly: In-app only. The ERP reads one mailbox and cannot send, so there is no email digest and no quiet hours — there is nothing to be quiet about. If that changes, this is where it will say so.

files.subtitle: Everything the system holds bytes for, next to the thing it arrived with. Files enter through the screen that knows what they are — the mailbox, the scanner, the importer — and are found again here.
files.none: Nothing yet. No attachment fetched, no dossier read, no workbook imported.

storage.title: Storage and files
storage.subtitle: Two places, and the real state of each — read off the disk, not off a counter.
storage.banner: Working files live on this machine. Finished documents are meant for SharePoint, where they would still open in File Explorer in three years without this application running. The second one is not wired up yet, and this page says so rather than rounding it off.
storage.notPermitted: The storage root and the list of orphaned files are infrastructure. This needs the company settings permission.

working.title: Working files — local disk
working.what: Fetched attachments, scanned dossiers, workbooks waiting to be imported. These are inputs: numerous, large, and nobody will ever want to open one from File Explorer in three years.
working.unwritableWhy: A file written now would not land. The folder may exist, but the system has no right to write in it — and finding that out at upload time is finding out too late.

drift.title: What the database believes, and what the disk holds
drift.agree: The two agree. {files} files claimed, {files} present.
drift.missing: {count} file(s) a row knows the path of, with no bytes behind it. Something was deleted underneath the system, or a write failed silently.
drift.orphaned: {count} file(s) on the disk ({size}) that no row claims. Harmless — but this is where the disk fills up from.
drift.nothingIsDeleted: This page deletes nothing. It reports. The same choice screen 83 makes for records: deleting is an act, not a side effect of a settings screen.

final.title: Finished documents — SharePoint
final.what: Issued offers, invoices and delivery notes, filed where they are already paid for, already backed up, and openable without this application.
final.needs: It needs the Graph permission {permission}, scoped to one site — the same conversation as the mailbox, and not yet had.
final.meanwhile: Meanwhile a PDF is rendered on demand from the document and its template. Nothing is lost; nothing is filed either.

bin.title: Byte bin
bin.why: Removing a file moves it here rather than unlinking it. The same rule as screen 83, applied to bytes instead of rows.

backup.title: Backup
backup.none: No backup has ever been taken, of this disk or of the database. Real mail, classifications and read state exist only here, on this machine. It is the largest single risk in the installation today.
backup.daysAgo: {days, plural, one {# day ago} other {# days ago}}
backup.how: Taken by scripts\server\backup.ps1, nightly. It restores each dump into a scratch database and compares every row before calling it good.
backup.failingWhy: The last run did not read its dump back, so nobody knows whether it can be restored. Run scripts\server\backup.ps1 by hand and read what it says.
backup.staleWhy: A backup runs every night. This one is older than that, so the scheduled task is not running. Check it: Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'SUPSERV backup'.
backup.sameDiskWhy: This backup is on the same disk as the database it protects. It covers a mistake and nothing else - not the disk, not the machine, not the room. Plug in the external drive and set BACKUP_LOCAL_PATH.
backup.drill: Prove it: scripts\server\restore.ps1 restores the newest dump into a scratch database and counts what comes back. Nothing live is touched.

emailTemplates.title: Email templates and snippets
emailTemplates.subtitle: {total} templates, {blank} of them still blank.
emailTemplates.doesNotSend: The ERP does not send. It holds Mail.Read and nothing more: a template produces text you copy into Outlook and send under your own name. That is also what Law 6 wants — the assistant proposes, it never executes.
emailTemplates.empty: The templates are not listed yet. Listing them writes no wording: each row arrives blank, with the moment it is for. Nothing is invented — a plausible covering note written by a machine ends up sent to a client by somebody who assumed a human wrote it.
emailTemplates.unknownRefused: A field outside the vocabulary is refused on save.
emailTemplates.vocabularyClosed: The list is closed. No condition, no loop, no function call: text edited from a settings screen must never be able to become code.
emailTemplates.languageIsTheirs: The language is the recipient's, not yours. Law 4: the interface follows the person, documents follow the counterparty.

error.notAllowed: This needs the company settings permission.
error.unknownPlaceholder: A field in braces is not part of the vocabulary. Check the spelling — otherwise it would go out in the email exactly as typed.

name.supplierRfq: Ask a supplier for a price

when.signature: At the foot of every email
when.bankDetails: With an invoice or a proforma

audit.title: Audit log
audit.subtitle: {total} entries, reaching back to {since}.
audit.banner: An audit entry outlives the record it describes: a company goes to the bin, the row may go after thirty days, and the entry saying it existed and why it went stays. This log records changes, and the reads that are themselves an act — fetching the mailbox. Opening a screen is not recorded.
audit.empty: Nothing has been recorded yet. The table fills itself: every creation, edit, issue and deletion writes a line here.
audit.notPermitted: This log holds everything — salaries, margins, who deleted what. It needs the company settings permission.

complianceNow.title: Compliance
complianceNow.subtitle: {confirmed} rule(s) refuse; {unconfirmed} only warn, because nobody has confirmed them.
complianceNow.cannotIssue: Nothing can be issued yet: {missing} is missing. That is not a compliance rule — it is day one, unfinished.
complianceNow.notALawyer: This software enforces rules; it does not assert that they are the law. Each one names its source and the person who confirmed it. None of this replaces your accountant.

drafts.title: What would happen at issue
drafts.allClear: All {count} drafts pass every rule that can be evaluated.
drafts.cashCaveat: Stamp duty depends on settlement in cash, and that is not a column on the document: it is a box ticked at the moment of issue. So the rule is not evaluated here, rather than reported as a pass it did not earn.

rules.title: The rules, and what they do

structural.title: Structural guarantees
structural.what: True because of how the system is built, not because anybody confirmed them. There is no switch.

assistantSafety.title: The assistant — what it can do
assistantSafety.subtitle: {available} of {total} tools are available to you.
assistantSafety.law6: Law 6: the assistant proposes, it never executes. This page renders the registry the runtime actually uses, not a description of it — if a tool is not listed here, it does not exist.
assistantSafety.neverWhy: Issuing and sending are absent because they are irreversible outside this building: a number is consumed, or a client reads something. Deleting is absent twice over — the permission is stripped from the assistant before the registry is even consulted.
assistantSafety.everyAnswerCited: Every answer points at the screen where the same row is visible. An answer you cannot check is a rumour with a link missing.
assistantSafety.proposalIsARow: A proposal is a row saying somebody might want to do this. Nothing changes until a person presses approve.
assistantSafety.identityWhat: Exactly you. It holds your permissions — you are {role} — minus the right to delete. It can see nothing you could not see by opening the screen yourself.
assistantSafety.noServiceAccount: No service account, no elevation. That is why this table changes depending on who is looking.
assistantSafety.byRoleWhy: Counted from the registry, not written by hand. A role with no permissions gets no tools, and that is the right answer.
assistantSafety.noModelWhat: What is late is arithmetic over a date and a balance. No model is called, and the company's correspondence does not leave this machine. See docs/DECISIONS/2026-08-28-the-assistant-does-not-guess.md.

tool.whatIsWaitingOnThem: What is waiting on other people
tool.whatWouldBeRefused: What would be refused at issue
tool.draftEnquiryReply: Draft a reply to an enquiry

proposals.title: Assistant proposals
proposals.subtitle: {waiting} waiting on a decision.
proposals.twoGates: Two gates, not one. Approving creates a record — never a send: the ERP holds only Mail.Read, and you send from Outlook. Nothing here goes out on its own.
proposals.decidedAndCreated: Approved. A reminder was created as a draft — it has not been sent.
proposals.noneWaiting: No proposals waiting. The assistant writes one only when asked — nothing runs in the background.
proposals.cannotDecide: Deciding this one needs the permission to issue invoices.
proposals.nothingRuns: This list is computed, not a queue. No background job writes proposals nobody asked for.

error.noTemplate: There is no reminder template in this client's language.
error.templateBlank: The reminder template is blank. The assistant does not invent SUPSERV's wording — write it first, in Settings → Email templates.
error.notPermitted: You do not hold the permission that needs.
error.noCitations: A proposal nobody can check is not a proposal.
error.alreadyDecided: That proposal has already been decided.
error.missingSubject: The proposal does not say what it is about.

assistantPage.title: The assistant
assistantPage.subtitle: What is late, and why. Every line links to the screen the fact came from.
assistantPage.nothingChecked: Nothing to examine yet — no deadlines, no invoices, no messages waiting.
assistantPage.arithmetic: Computed from dates and balances. No language model is involved and nothing leaves this machine.
assistantPage.waitingOnOthers: {count} things are waiting on other people —
assistantPage.noProposals: No proposals waiting. The assistant writes one only when asked.
assistantPage.cannotDoWhat: Issue, send, take payment, delete, change permissions, confirm a compliance rule. None of it exists in its registry.

reports.title: Reports
reports.subtitle: Everything is computed when the page is drawn. No total is stored.
reports.nothingIssuedYet: No document has been issued yet. These reports fill themselves — there is nothing to configure.
reports.wonHow: Won is not a tick box: it is a client order arriving. The figure is counted off the documents, not off a flag somebody has to remember to set.
reports.draftsAreNotSales: A draft is not a sale
reports.computedNow: These figures are recomputed on every view. A stored total is a total that can disagree with the rows it claims to summarise, and nobody notices which of the two is wrong.

dashboard.subtitle: What matters today, seen as {role}.
dashboard.moneyHidden: Collection figures are not shown: they need the permission to issue invoices. Not greyed out — on a dashboard a greyed bar still gives away an order of magnitude by its width.
dashboard.nothingIssuedYet: No document has been issued yet. The figures fill themselves once day one is done.

orders.subtitle: What clients ordered from us, and what we ordered from suppliers. Two directions, one list.

dealItems.title: Item list
dealItems.subtitle: {client} · {count} line(s)
dealItems.noLines: No lines. Paste the client's request below.
dealItems.pasteLabel: Paste here — reference, designation, quantity, unit
dealItems.howItReads: The text is re-read by the server, not taken from the table shown: what the browser displayed is what a person SAW, and that is not evidence of what the text says. Tabs, numbered lines and dashes are all recognised.
dealItems.affects: Captured prices and technical coverage hang off the lines. Replacing the list unhooks them — deliberately: a line that changed no longer has the same price.

error.nothingToAdd: Nothing to save: the pasted text holds no readable line.
error.closed: This enquiry is lost. Editing what the client asked for would rewrite history.

itemTechnical.nothingHeld: Nothing is held on this item yet. This is what the technical annexe will ask for on the first enquiry that needs it.
itemTechnical.usedOnWhy: A datasheet found once serves the next time
itemTechnical.neverAsked: No enquiry has asked for this item yet.
itemTechnical.gathering: Pieces gather across enquiries. Nothing here is invented: every row was recorded by somebody, with its provenance.

modules.title: Modules
modules.subtitle: {built} built, {parked} deliberately parked.
modules.noSwitches: There are no switches, deliberately. Turning a module off would have to mean something: either the screens vanish — and somebody who opened Deliveries yesterday cannot find them, while the rows stay in the database being counted by every report — or the screens stay and the switch does nothing, which is a lie with a toggle on it.
modules.parkedWhy: Not coming soon: a decision written into the plan, §7. The system does not do these things, and saying so beats letting somebody find out.

forms.title: Website intake forms
forms.subtitle: An intake channel that does not exist yet, and why.
forms.whyNotBuilt: What is missing is not the form. It is a public endpoint on a machine that today answers only through Cloudflare Access: every request is authenticated at the edge, which is exactly what a public form must not be. That is an infrastructure decision, not a UI one.

need.publicEndpoint: One public path, excluded from Cloudflare Access, and only that one — the rest of the ERP stays closed.
need.spam: Filtering: a public address receives spam from the first day.
need.routing: A routing rule, like screen 38's, to say what an arriving message becomes.

forms.meanwhileWhat: Enquiries arrive at contact@supserv-dz.com and show up in the Inbox. Nothing is lost — it is an email address rather than a form.

banner.held: The supplier invoice is {amount} above the purchase order. Nothing is paid until you decide whether that difference is agreed.
banner.quantity: The supplier has invoiced more than has arrived. Nothing is paid until the two are reconciled.

lines.title: Ordered from the supplier
lines.how: received and remaining are counted off the goods receipts, never typed

receipts.title: Goods received
receipts.how: what actually arrived, not what was ordered
receipts.none: Nothing has arrived against this order yet. Until a goods receipt exists, every quantity in the Received column is nought and the client delivery date is a guess.

match.title: Three-way match
match.how: purchase order · goods received · supplier invoice
match.nothingIsPaid: Nothing is paid until a difference is settled. Either the supplier repriced without telling us, or it is a different article — both are questions for a person, and neither is a reason to hold up the lines that are correct.

owed.title: What we owe them
owed.terms: Their terms: {terms}. What has actually been paid is read from the bank, not from the terms.
owed.noTerms: No payment terms are recorded against this supplier. Screen 22 is where they go, and every offer and invoice reads them from there.

blocks.title: What this blocks
blocks.deliverReceived: Deliver {count} complete lines to the client
blocks.deliverNotReceived: Deliver {count} lines that have not arrived
blocks.why: This is the leg that was missing. Without it the client delivery date is a guess and the margin is whatever the supplier decides to invoice.

invoices.title: Supplier invoices
invoices.theirNumber: Numbered by the supplier, never by us — the number on the paper is the one everybody quotes.

tenders.summary: {open, plural, one {# open} other {# open}} · {closing, plural, =0 {none closing within 48 hours} one {# closing within 48 hours} other {# closing within 48 hours}} · {incomplete, plural, =0 {every folder complete} one {# folder incomplete} other {# folders incomplete}}
tenders.none: No tenders yet. A tender is an enquiry answering a formal procedure — open the enquiry and record the procedure, the place of deposit and the bid bond, and it appears here with its folder.

tender.banner: Dossier {percent}% complete. {blocking, plural, one {# item will have the bid rejected} other {# items will have the bid rejected}} if it is deposited as it is.

piece.rc_copy: Copy of the registre de commerce
piece.comptes_sociaux: Attestation de dépôt des comptes sociaux

tender.noPieces: This tender's folder is empty. The pieces are whatever its cahier des charges asks for — nothing here asserts what the law requires.

blocking.title: Blocking now
blocking.why: Missing, expired, or valid today and expired on the day of the deposit. The date that decides is not today.

tender.thisIsAnEnquiryWhy: A tender is a deal with a procedure. The client, the lines, the offer and the outcome all live on the enquiry, and every screen that reads them reads the same record.

projects.summary: {active, plural, one {# active} other {# active}} · {warranty, plural, =0 {none in warranty} one {# in warranty} other {# in warranty}} · {retention} held in retenue de garantie
projects.none: No projects yet. A project is what happens after a deal is won — the situations, the retention and the bank guarantees. Open the enquiry and start one.
projects.waitingBanner: Situation n°{n} on {code} has been with {client} for {days} days without approval. Payment cannot start until it is signed.

project.fromEnquiryWhy: Every project belongs to a deal. The client, the offer and the order that started the work all live there, and nothing about this site is recorded twice.

situations.title: Situations / attachements
situations.none: No situation has been raised yet. A situation is a document of kind `situation` against this project — the same engine as every other document.

crew.title: Crew on site
crew.none: Nobody is recorded on this site. The people come from screen 51 and their tickets come with them.

progress.ahead: {points} points of work done and not yet billed. That is money already spent and not asked for.
progress.level: Billing has caught up with the work.
progress.noEstimate: Nobody has estimated physical progress. Financial progress alone says what has been signed off, not what has been built.

basis.definitive: Counted from the PV de réception définitive.
basis.provisional: A projection off the provisional acceptance. It is not a date anybody has agreed to until the PV définitif exists.
basis.unknown: No release date can be worked out until the work is accepted and a warranty period is recorded.

cautions.title: Cautions
cautions.why: A lapsed guarantee can be called in by the client — they draw on it and we argue afterwards. A bank takes about six weeks to renew one.

cautionBanner.expiresBeforeAcceptance: The {kind} guarantee expires {on} — before provisional acceptance. Renew it or the client can call it in.
cautionBanner.lapsed: The {kind} guarantee lapsed on {on}. Until it is renewed the client is holding an unsecured contract.
cautionBanner.expiring: The {kind} guarantee expires {on}. A bank takes about six weeks to renew one.

candidates.title: Candidates
candidates.subtitle: {n} people in the pipeline · {expiring} certifications expiring
candidates.none: Nobody matches this filter. A candidate is a person whose relationship is `candidate` — the same table as everybody else on a site.
candidates.expiringBanner: {n, plural, one {# site certification expires} other {# site certifications expire}} within {days} days. A ticket running out under a man who is working is worth more attention than one under a CV nobody has read.

candidate.samePersonWhy: A candidate is a row in the people table. Hiring them changes one field — they keep their trade, their number and every certification already attached, and nothing is copied anywhere.

certifications.title: Certifications
certifications.why: the soonest to expire decides which sites they can go to
certifications.none: No certification is recorded. That is normal for a manœuvre and it is a problem for a welder on a TouatGaz site.

considered.title: Being considered for
considered.none: Not on any shortlist. Screen 26 is where a request puts somebody forward.

requests.summary: {open, plural, one {# open} other {# open}} · {positions, plural, =0 {every position filled} one {# position to fill} other {# positions to fill}} · {soon, plural, =0 {none needed this week} one {# needed within 7 days} other {# needed within 7 days}}
requests.none: No personnel request matches this filter. A request is a site asking for people by a date — not a job advertisement.
requests.banner: {ref} needs {needed} {role} in {wilaya} in {days} days and has {usable} who can actually go. The rest are confirmed with a certification that expires before the start date.

shortlist.title: Shortlist — {ref} · {needed} {role}, {wilaya}
shortlist.certificationMandatory: certification is mandatory for this site
shortlist.noCertificationNeeded: no certification required for this site

scorecard.bouncedNote: {n} messages bounced and are kept out of the reply rate
scorecard.fromAsked: from the day we asked to the day they answered
scorecard.vsOthers: against other suppliers who priced the same line
scorecard.nothingStoredWhy: There is no rating field. Every figure is arithmetic over the requests we sent, what they answered and whether the offer built on their price was won — so a supplier who stops replying shows it the following month, without anybody remembering to update anything.

prices.title: Price history
prices.how: the last price they quoted, per reference
prices.none: They have never quoted a price. A supplier with no history is a supplier nobody has asked, which is its own answer.

requests.title: Recent requests
requests.none: This supplier has never been on a sourcing request.

bpu.title: Schedule of prices — {n} lines
bpu.noDraftOffer: No draft offer on this enquiry yet. Start one from the enquiry.
bpu.banner: {lines} lines imported without retyping. {known} of them we have priced before — the last price we paid is shown so you are not starting from zero.

empty.title: No lines yet
empty.body: The bordereau arrives as a spreadsheet. It is read here, column by column, and confirmed by a person — nothing is imported on a guess.

mapping.title: Column mapping
mapping.once: confirm once — remembered for this client
mapping.idle: Upload the client's bordereau. The columns are proposed from their headings and you confirm them: a column called “Montant” read as a unit price puts a wrong figure on a submitted bid.

problem.noLineNumber: Row {row}: no line number — not imported.
problem.unreadableQuantity: Row {row}: quantity could not be read — not imported.
problem.duplicateLine: Row {row}: that line number is already used — not imported.

erratum.title: Erratum
erratum.noneWhy: When the buyer issues a corrected bordereau, upload it here. It is diffed line by line against what is held, and nothing moves until somebody applies it.
erratum.explain: {repriced} lines keep their price — a quantity change does not change a unit price. {losing} lose it: a designation or a unit that changes names a different article.
erratum.issued: An offer has already gone out against the previous bordereau ({numbers}). It will not be amended — an issued document does not change. Tick below to apply the erratum knowing that.
erratum.acknowledge: Apply it knowing an issued offer carries the old quantities.
erratum.detachWhy: Supplier prices on lines that change are not deleted: they are stamped stale as of the day the erratum is applied. What a supplier quoted in August stays as evidence of what the valve cost then.

totals.title: Totals
totals.hidden: cost and margin hidden from Commercial
totals.partial: These totals cover the {priced} priced lines out of {lines}. They are not the value of the offer.

history.title: History helps here
history.why: Measured over the {lines} lines where we know both the last price paid and a cost today.

sources.title: Files read
sources.none: No file has been read for this enquiry yet.

error.notAllowed: Pricing a bordereau means seeing costs. Your role does not allow it.
error.noBatch: That file is no longer available. Upload it again.
error.noSuchBatch: That file is no longer available. Upload it again.
error.alreadyImported: This enquiry already has lines. A second file is an erratum: upload it from the Erratum tab, where it is compared line by line.
error.nothingImportedYet: Import the bordereau first — there is nothing to compare against.
error.unreadable: That file could not be read.
error.emptySheet: The first sheet of that file is empty.
error.mappingIncomplete: At least the line number, the designation or the quantity is missing. Without those three it is not a bordereau.
error.noLines: No readable lines in that file.
error.nothingChanged: This erratum changes nothing against the lines held.
error.erratumAlreadyPending: An erratum is already waiting. Deal with it before uploading another.
error.erratumNotPending: That erratum has already been dealt with.
error.offerAlreadyIssued: An offer has already gone out against the previous bordereau. Tick the box to apply the erratum knowing that.
